title: How a Series Of Emails From Francis Ford Coppola Led Electronic Artist Dan Deacon To Film Scoring: ‘It Was Never My Goal To Be a Touring Musician’
summary: The Baltimore musician made his name with his vibrant electronic records and energetic live shows — but now, listeners are most likely to hear his compositions in hit movies and TV shows.
body: In 2009, about a month after appearing on NPR to promote his new album, the experimental electronic musician Dan Deacon received an email from the legendary director Francis Ford Coppola — or at least, someone claiming to be him. The sender’s email address had “a bunch of letters and numbers that looked like spam,” Deacon says. “I think it’s a new, Nigerian prince, you’ve got $43 million [scam]. I’m like, ‘There’s no way this is real,’ so I ignore it. “A week goes by, and I get another email from a different email address that has a similar, just bizarre nature to it. It’s like, ‘Trying to reach you, this is Francis Ford Coppola, I would love to connect,'” continues Deacon, who once again ignored the note. Eventually, Deacon received an email affiliated with the consulate of Belize — where Coppola is an honorary consul — reiterating the ask. After Deacon gut-checked with his agent, he responded, and the film giant invited the musician, then in his late twenties, to his estate in Napa, California. Listening to Deacon’s NPR interview, Coppola had been struck by a tangent he’d gone on…

title: Reddit is letting AI decide when your post breaks the rules
summary: The machines are moving into the mod queue, and they can be given the power to delete your posts.
body: Credit: Edgar Cervantes / Android Authority TL;DR Reddit’s new Rules Hub uses AI to judge whether posts and comments violate the “intent” of subreddit rules. Moderators decide whether suspected violations are flagged for review or removed automatically. The optional tool is rolling out more widely later in 2026, following testing in over 700 communities. Reddit moderation has never exactly been a polished operation. It runs on volunteer moderators, user reports, and Automod rules that may have been written years ago by someone who has since vanished from the subreddit. Perhaps inevitably, AI is now also being invited behind the scenes at Reddit, with a new system that can decide whether posts and comments should be reported or removed. As The Verge reports, Reddit’s new Rules Hub uses large language models to judge whether content matches the “intent” of a subreddit rule. Automod usually looks for specific words, phrases, or patterns, while the new system is meant to understand context and handle messier cases that don’t fit neatly into a keyword filter.
